name: Video Streaming Advertising Lens
description: This paper describes the Video Streaming Advertising (VSA) Lens for the AWS Well-Architected Framework. The lens explores how to review and improve your cloud-based architectures and better understand the impact of design decisions for advertising workloads. We present general design principles and specific best practices aligned to the six pillars of the Well-Architected Framework.

questions.title: How do you govern advertising workloads and assign accountability across architecture, data, yield, and campaign operations?
questions.description: Advertising workloads require clear decision rights across architecture, data, campaign operations, and revenue protection. Linear and digital teams need shared accountability for technical health and campaign outcomes, especially when one commercial commitment crosses several delivery systems. This capability defines the organizational mechanisms and common operating model for those decisions.

choices.title: Assess trade-offs between ad serving architecture options and associated risks

helpfulResource.displayText: When you design ad-serving infrastructure, evaluate the trade-offs between architectural options and their risks. Consider performance, scalability, availability, security, and cost. For publisher workloads, also evaluate server-guided ad insertion (SGAI) patterns, prebid deployment topologies, and free ad-supported streaming TV (FAST) channel assembly approaches. Do this through structured trade-off workshops that produce documented architecture decision records (ADRs).

improvementPlan.displayText: Assess trade-offs between ad serving architecture options and associated risks

choices.title: Create RACI matrices that define the roles and responsibilities for each key advertising process

helpfulResource.displayText: Define stakeholder roles so key advertising processes run without handoff gaps. Use RACI (responsible, accountable, consulted, and informed) matrices to assign accountability and decisions for publisher-specific workloads (SGAI manifest pipelines, prebid adapter onboarding, and FAST channel scheduling) and for converged linear and digital operations.

improvementPlan.displayText: Create RACI matrices that define the roles and responsibilities for each key advertising process

choices.title: Establish performance metrics by defining key performance indicators (KPIs) and service-level objectives (SLOs)

helpfulResource.displayText: Establishing a set of operational performance metrics helps organizations monitor and validate the performance of advertising operations. KPIs and SLOs must extend beyond infrastructure availability to cover publisher yield health (eCPM, fill rate, bids per auction, ad break completion, and identity-signal match rates) and tie operational health directly to revenue outcomes.

improvementPlan.displayText: Establish performance metrics by defining key performance indicators (KPIs) and service-level objectives (SLOs)

choices.title: Establish data governance and compliance operations

helpfulResource.displayText: Advertising data management requires governance and compliance procedures for Multi-Region environments, where regional privacy laws vary by jurisdiction. Procedures must cover application logs, managed connectivity service logs, and agentic AI agent traces.

improvementPlan.displayText: Establish data governance and compliance operations

choices.title: Foster a publisher operations culture that prioritizes yield reliability

helpfulResource.displayText: Build a culture that treats yield reliability with the same urgency as system availability. This best practice addresses how teams proactively monitor monetization health and treat revenue-impacting incidents with defined severity classifications, using shared dashboards visible to both engineering and ad operations, and escalation paths that mirror infrastructure incident severity levels.

improvementPlan.displayText: Foster a publisher operations culture that prioritizes yield reliability

choices.title: Implement a unified campaign management interface across linear and digital operations

helpfulResource.displayText: Establish a single, integrated campaign management system that provides unified visibility and control across linear TV scheduling and digital and CTV programmatic operations. This removes the need for parallel ad ops teams running disconnected workflows by converging campaign booking, trafficking, delivery monitoring, and reconciliation into one operational interface.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement a unified campaign management interface across linear and digital operations

questions.title: How do you observe advertising workload health and connect technical signals to delivery and revenue outcomes?
questions.description: Advertising delivery depends on distributed systems, partner connections, automated decisions, and channel-specific fulfillment paths. Operators need correlated telemetry across technical and business layers to identify whether a failure affects infrastructure, auction behavior, campaign pacing, or revenue. This capability defines the observability needed to detect, diagnose, and route those conditions.

choices.title: Implement monitoring across each layer of your advertising stack

helpfulResource.displayText: Operational excellence in advertising workloads requires monitoring across ad-serving infrastructure, data pipelines, application performance, user experience, partner connectivity, and agentic AI. For publisher workloads, this includes sell-side monitoring on monetization, content delivery pipeline (SGAI), playout health (FAST), and rendering health for innovative ad formats. With a multi-layered approach, you can detect and resolve problems before they affect revenue or the viewer. You can also correlate signals across tiers.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement monitoring across each layer of your advertising stack

choices.title: Collect and analyze detailed metrics for successful operations and ad campaigns

helpfulResource.displayText: Advertising workloads spike in traffic and resource use, and both performance and yield vary with them. To keep observability across shifting workloads, collect granular, near-real-time metrics across every tier: infrastructure, application, partner connectivity, database, agentic AI, and (for publisher workloads) monetization, SGAI delivery, and FAST playout. Segment metrics by partner and adapter, apply anomaly detection, and tier alarms to business outcomes so issues surface before they hit bid win rate or campaign delivery.

improvementPlan.displayText: Collect and analyze detailed metrics for successful operations and ad campaigns

choices.title: Implement centralized logging to aggregate logs from all components of your advertising stack

helpfulResource.displayText: Aggregate logs from every component of your advertising stack into a centralized store. Aggregate logs from components such as third-party integrations, custom applications, managed connectivity services, and agentic AI workflows.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement centralized logging to aggregate logs from all components of your advertising stack

choices.title: Instrument your advertising application code and infrastructure to emit detailed, structured logs and metrics

helpfulResource.displayText: Instrument your advertising application code and infrastructure to emit detailed, structured logs and metrics. Operations teams can then see into every tier of the ad-serving stack. Structured instrumentation helps teams detect and resolve issues quickly, and scales with complex systems such as managed connectivity and agent-based decision-making. Extend instrumentation to capture the correlation between network events and application outcomes.

improvementPlan.displayText: Instrument your advertising application code and infrastructure to emit detailed, structured logs and metrics

choices.title: Monitor partner connectivity health and traffic management effectiveness across your advertising network

helpfulResource.displayText: Advertising workloads depend on low-latency connectivity with tens to hundreds of external partners. Monitor the health, latency, and throughput of each partner connection in both your network and application. When traffic management modules such as rate limiting and request filtering are applied in the connectivity path, monitor their effectiveness to validate that controls work as intended and to distinguish between network-generated and application-generated responses.

improvementPlan.displayText: Monitor partner connectivity health and traffic management effectiveness across your advertising network

choices.title: Implement distributed tracing for automated and agent-driven advertising operations

helpfulResource.displayText: As advertising operations increasingly use AI agents for bid optimization, creative selection, campaign management, and brand safety monitoring, implement distributed tracing to maintain visibility into multi-step automated workflows. Distributed tracing enables rapid root cause analysis when automated decisions produce unexpected outcomes and provides an audit trail for agent-driven actions across the advertising value chain.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement distributed tracing for automated and agent-driven advertising operations

choices.title: Implement observability for bot and agent traffic in AI content licensing

helpfulResource.displayText: AI search agents are reducing direct traffic to publisher sites and cutting ad revenue, while AI-powered bots can generate false impressions that constitute ad tech fraud. You need real-time visibility into bot and agent traffic volumes, classification accuracy, and revenue impact. Automated detection identifies anomalous bot behavior patterns that may indicate ad fraud or unauthorized content crawling.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement observability for bot and agent traffic in AI content licensing

choices.title: Monitor server-side auction health and demand partner yield across your header bidding infrastructure

helpfulResource.displayText: Server-side header bidding runs a parallel auction among configured demand partners, replacing the sequential waterfall model with a single, instrumentable decision point. Monitor auction-level health and yield by demand partner to determine whether your demand configuration maximizes publisher revenue.

improvementPlan.displayText: Monitor server-side auction health and demand partner yield across your header bidding infrastructure

choices.title: Implement centralized observability for campaign delivery pacing and fulfillment across linear and digital channels

helpfulResource.displayText: Deploy a unified observability stack that provides real-time visibility into campaign delivery, pacing, and fulfillment metrics across both linear TV schedules and digital programmatic pipelines. Use KPI-driven monitoring with anomaly detection to identify delivery issues before they impact campaign outcomes.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement centralized observability for campaign delivery pacing and fulfillment across linear and digital channels

questions.title: How do you prepare advertising workload changes and launches for safe production operation?
questions.description: Publisher changes can alter auction competition, manifest behavior, channel schedules, and partner demand without causing an immediate service outage. Teams need release controls that reflect how each change propagates, formal evidence that a workload is ready for production, and ongoing management of external integrations. This capability defines how teams prepare, validate, release, and reassess those changes.

choices.title: Mitigate deployment risks for publisher workload changes

helpfulResource.displayText: Controlled deployment mechanisms help publishers reduce the risk of deploying changes to Prebid adapter configurations, SGAI manifest generation logic, FAST channel schedules, and ad format rendering code. These mechanisms limit the scope of impact of bad deployments and enable rapid rollback.

improvementPlan.displayText: Mitigate deployment risks for publisher workload changes

choices.title: Establish operational readiness reviews for publisher launches

helpfulResource.displayText: New SSP adapter integrations, SGAI pipeline deployments, FAST channel launches, and innovative ad format rollouts must undergo an operational readiness review before entering production. The review is a formal gate. A workload that fails any checklist item must not activate.

improvementPlan.displayText: Establish operational readiness reviews for publisher launches

choices.title: Design publisher workloads to reduce defects and improve flow

helpfulResource.displayText: Design Prebid, SGAI, FAST channel, and ad format workloads to minimize defects through automated testing, configuration validation, and progressive delivery. Treat all workload configurations as code. Use version control, automated linting, and integration testing to prevent configuration errors from reaching production.

improvementPlan.displayText: Design publisher workloads to reduce defects and improve flow

choices.title: Establish third-party DSP integration operations for Prebid Server

helpfulResource.displayText: Third-party DSP integrations require dedicated operational management beyond standard adapter onboarding. Each DSP can support different identity frameworks (UID2, LiveRamp, and ID5) with varying signal fidelity. The operational health of these integrations affects bid response rates and publisher yield in a multi-identity-provider environment.

improvementPlan.displayText: Establish third-party DSP integration operations for Prebid Server

questions.title: How do you manage operational processes and respond consistently to advertising workload events and incidents?
questions.description: Advertising operations must match response mechanisms to failure predictability, data urgency, and revenue impact while maintaining one incident process across linear and digital channels. Teams need documented and automated response paths, measurement of process effectiveness, and controlled real-time decisions that remain correct under load. This capability covers production operations after launch rather than change readiness.

choices.title: Create runbooks for the most common operational events and incidents that can impact your advertising workload

helpfulResource.displayText: Develop structured procedures to manage operational events and incidents in your advertising workloads. Runbooks provide step-by-step procedures for well-understood, routine operations, while playbooks guide your response to incidents with less predictable outcomes. For a publisher workload, runbooks cover Prebid adapter timeout escalation, SGAI manifest errors, FAST channel outages, converged linear and digital incident scenarios, and infrastructure capacity events ahead of high-traffic advertising moments.

improvementPlan.displayText: Create runbooks for the most common operational events and incidents that can impact your advertising workload

choices.title: Automate runbooks to gain operational efficiency

helpfulResource.displayText: Document runbooks for failover, capacity scaling, and incident response workflows, then encode them as executable automation documents. For publisher workloads, automate high-frequency responses including adapter failover, SGAI manifest regeneration, FAST channel content gap remediation, and ad pod backfill.

improvementPlan.displayText: Automate runbooks to gain operational efficiency

choices.title: Monitor and manage the health of publisher operations processes

helpfulResource.displayText: Beyond workload health, track the health of operational processes: incident response efficiency, runbook execution accuracy, and on-call rotation effectiveness.

improvementPlan.displayText: Monitor and manage the health of publisher operations processes

choices.title: Establish AdOps measurement for shoppable ad fulfillment and non-intrusive ads

helpfulResource.displayText: Shoppable ads use an embedding-based matching pipeline that matches image embeddings to content embeddings in an ecommerce vector store based on similarity scores. Non-intrusive ads (squeezebacks, overlays, and pause ads) operate outside conventional click-through attribution. Shoppable and non-intrusive ads require measurement approaches distinct from conventional ad attribution to demonstrate effectiveness to advertisers.

improvementPlan.displayText: Establish AdOps measurement for shoppable ad fulfillment and non-intrusive ads

choices.title: Implement event-driven automation for ad placement decisions across linear logs and digital bid streams

helpfulResource.displayText: Deploy event-driven architectures that react to state changes in linear broadcast schedules and digital programmatic bid streams to automate ad placement decisions in real time. Use loosely coupled microservices with asynchronous event processing for deterministic, scalable ad serving across converged environments.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement event-driven automation for ad placement decisions across linear logs and digital bid streams

choices.title: Implement operational procedures based on data classification and latency requirements

helpfulResource.displayText: Establish tier-based procedures for low-latency data (bid requests), medium-latency data (campaign optimization), and high-latency data (historical analytics). Classify managed connectivity service metrics as low-latency operational data, and agentic AI agent traces as medium-latency operational data.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement operational procedures based on data classification and latency requirements

choices.title: Standardize incident response and escalation procedures across linear playout and digital ad serving

helpfulResource.displayText: Establish a unified incident response framework with consistent classification, escalation, and remediation procedures that apply across linear broadcast playout and digital ad serving infrastructure. Use automated detection, tiered escalation, and runbook automation to minimize MTTR across converged operations.

improvementPlan.displayText: Standardize incident response and escalation procedures across linear playout and digital ad serving

questions.title: How do you achieve operational reliability and observability for your server-guided ad insertion pipeline?
questions.description: This capability focuses primarily on the hybrid SGAI pattern given its CDN-caching implications and broader scope of impact for operational failures. The goal is full visibility into the SGAI pipeline from manifest creation through ad delivery, with automated alerting on ad break completion failures.

choices.title: Implement manifest generation observability with SCTE-35 marker validation

helpfulResource.displayText: Validate every generated SGAI manifest for SCTE-35 marker integrity before CDN distribution. In hybrid SGAI architectures, manifest errors move through CDN caching layers to every viewer of cached content.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement manifest generation observability with SCTE-35 marker validation

choices.title: Implement observability for ad break orchestration across server and client

helpfulResource.displayText: Because SGAI is hybrid, failures can occur at the server manifest, CDN caching, or client ad fetch layer, so you need cross-component observability to distinguish between failure origins. To identify root causes quickly, maintain full visibility from server-side manifest generation through CDN-cached delivery to client-side personalized ad fetching.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement observability for ad break orchestration across server and client

choices.title: Create SGAI-specific runbooks and playbooks for manifest and player failures

helpfulResource.displayText: Without documented response procedures, SGAI incidents require unplanned troubleshooting across multiple system layers (manifest generation, CDN caching, and client-side ad fetching), which extends MTTR and compounds revenue impact. Use runbooks for known failure modes and playbooks for novel failure patterns.

improvementPlan.displayText: Create SGAI-specific runbooks and playbooks for manifest and player failures

questions.title: How do you maintain operational health and ongoing improvement for FAST channel workloads?
questions.description: Free Ad-Supported Streaming TV (FAST) channels turn back-catalog content into ad-supported linear channels that run around the clock, so their operational health has to be tracked continuously. This capability covers the operational demands of linear streaming infrastructure: intelligent scheduling, content licensing workflows, ad fill optimization, and playout monitoring. It spans continuous readiness, observability for scheduling, fill, and playout, and ongoing KPI tracking and operational cadences.

choices.title: Establish continual linear streaming operational readiness

helpfulResource.displayText: FAST channels operate continuously without natural maintenance windows. Any playout interruption affects viewer experience and ad revenue with no opportunity to defer recovery. Before a FAST channel begins serving viewers, validate its operational readiness, including multi-AZ failover testing and EPG completeness validation.

improvementPlan.displayText: Establish continual linear streaming operational readiness

choices.title: Implement observability for scheduling, ad fill, and playout health

helpfulResource.displayText: FAST channel operations require observability across scheduling accuracy (is content playing as scheduled), ad fill health (are ad pods being filled at expected rates), and playout continuity (is the stream available and playing without interruption). Each of these areas requires its own metrics and alerts, and correlating signals across the three areas identifies the root cause when problems occur.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement observability for scheduling, ad fill, and playout health

choices.title: Establish FAST channel KPI dashboards and operational cadences

helpfulResource.displayText: Without dedicated KPI tracking and regular operational reviews, FAST channel performance degrades undetected until revenue drops or viewers churn. Dedicated dashboards and weekly cross-functional reviews create the visibility and accountability to maintain monetization health across continual linear streaming operations.

improvementPlan.displayText: Establish FAST channel KPI dashboards and operational cadences

questions.title: How do you continuously improve publisher monetization operations through feedback loops, experimentation, and learning?
questions.description: The standard Well-Architected OE pillar includes an Evolve area focused on learning, sharing, and improving (OPS11). This capability maps those nine OPS11 best practices to publisher yield optimization: ongoing improvement feedback loops, game days and failure injection exercises, A/B testing frameworks for ad format experimentation, post-incident reviews for revenue-affecting events, and knowledge sharing across publisher workload teams. Organizations that design advertising workloads should adopt practices that improve yield through continual refinement, safe experimentation, and learning from failures.

choices.title: Implement ongoing yield optimization feedback loops

helpfulResource.displayText: Publisher yield optimization requires feedback loops that help you inform your improvement initiatives through your operational data. Without them, publishers respond only after revenue drops occur. You can build automated yield reporting pipelines on AWS analytics services to reveal optimization opportunities early.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement ongoing yield optimization feedback loops

choices.title: Conduct game days and failure injection exercises

helpfulResource.displayText: Regular game days with realistic failure scenarios (SSP adapter outages, manifest generation failures, FAST channel playout interruptions, and innovative ad format rendering degradation) expose monitoring and runbook gaps before they cost revenue.

improvementPlan.displayText: Conduct game days and failure injection exercises

choices.title: Establish A/B testing frameworks for ad format experimentation

helpfulResource.displayText: With an A/B testing framework, you can safely test new ad formats (such as overlays, squeezebacks, pause ads, and shoppable ads), placement strategies, and auction configurations.

improvementPlan.displayText: Establish A/B testing frameworks for ad format experimentation

choices.title: Conduct post-incident reviews for revenue-affecting events

helpfulResource.displayText: Many publisher operations teams conduct post-incident reviews only for availability incidents while revenue-affecting events that did not cause visible downtime go unreviewed. Yield-affecting failure patterns repeat without systematic analysis or improvement. The operational excellence pillar specifies that post-incident analysis should review customer-affecting events, identify contributing factors and preventative actions, and develop mitigations to limit recurrence.

improvementPlan.displayText: Conduct post-incident reviews for revenue-affecting events

choices.title: Share operational knowledge across publisher workload teams

helpfulResource.displayText: Siloed teams operating Prebid, SGAI, FAST channel, and ad format workloads miss opportunities to apply cross-organization operational improvements. Many operational patterns, such ascanary deployment strategies, automated rollback procedures, yield anomaly detection approaches, apply across multiple publisher workload types. Systematic knowledge sharing helps your teams apply organizationally-tested outcomes, which improves time and revenue cost.

improvementPlan.displayText: Share operational knowledge across publisher workload teams

questions.title: How do you manage identities, access control, and authorization across your advertising platform and its programmatic partners?
questions.description: Access management for an advertising platform protects sensitive data, financial information, and programmatic access while keeping permissions appropriate for authorized users. Advertising platforms face a dual authentication challenge. Human users (campaign managers, traffickers, and analysts) need interactive identity flows, while machine-to-machine traffic (bid requests, creative syncs, and reporting APIs) requires low-latency token validation that doesn't exceed the 100 ms bid response window. Additional challenges arise from converged linear and digital environments, where panel data and census-level data must be governed with strict consent and identity boundaries.

choices.title: Implement user authentication and access control to protect bidding process and content

helpfulResource.displayText: Programmatic advertising platforms process authentication decisions for bid requests, creative uploads, and reporting interfaces. These decisions occur at high volume and within strict bid-response deadlines. Without authentication patterns designed for real-time bidding, unauthorized parties might access bid streams, campaign data, or audience segments.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement user authentication and access control to protect bidding process and content

choices.title: Restrict DSP access to allow only authorized SSPs

helpfulResource.displayText: In programmatic advertising, DSPs receive bid requests from dozens to hundreds of SSP partners. Without ingress controls that validate each SSP connection, unauthorized parties can submit fraudulent bid requests, access bidding signals, or send invalid traffic. That traffic consumes compute resources without generating revenue.

improvementPlan.displayText: Restrict DSP access to allow only authorized SSPs

choices.title: Restrict DSP outbound traffic to authorized SSPs only

helpfulResource.displayText: DSPs transmit bid responses containing pricing signals, audience segment data, and creative selection decisions to SSP endpoints. If outbound traffic isn't restricted to authorized destinations, this data can leak to unauthorized parties and expose competitive intelligence.

improvementPlan.displayText: Restrict DSP outbound traffic to authorized SSPs only

choices.title: Implement least privilege access to protect programmatic workloads

helpfulResource.displayText: Ad tech systems process data across organizational boundaries where advertisers, publishers, agencies, and measurement vendors each require different access scopes. Without authorization policies that reflect advertising-specific data boundaries, authenticated users can access campaign data, audience segments, or financial information outside their business relationship.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement least privilege access to protect programmatic workloads

choices.title: Implement cross-platform identity governance for converged linear and digital operations

helpfulResource.displayText: The unified platform of linear television and digital advertising means that identity governance must cover two unique data models: household panels and user-level impressions. Without it, identity resolution can expose viewer data across consent boundaries or reveal panel membership to unauthorized parties.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement cross-platform identity governance for converged linear and digital operations

questions.title: How do you protect advertising data throughout transit, storage, collaboration, and computation?
questions.description: This capability covers protection in transit, at rest, during collaboration, and during record-level computation. It doesn't define identity governance or decide which regulatory obligations apply.

choices.title: Encrypt DSP to SSP communication in transit using TLS

helpfulResource.displayText: Programmatic advertising bid traffic crosses organizational and network boundaries between independent companies with their own infrastructure. Application-layer encryption is the only mechanism that can protect this traffic across those boundaries. Network-layer controls that secure traffic within one organization do not address the cross-organization threat model.

improvementPlan.displayText: Encrypt DSP to SSP communication in transit using TLS

choices.title: Protect linear distribution feeds and ad signaling in converged delivery

helpfulResource.displayText: When linear broadcast workflows converge with cloud-based ad insertion, SCTE-35 markers move from physically secured facilities to IP contribution links and programmable control planes. Without transport and control-plane integrity, unauthorized parties can insert or suppress ad breaks and affect monetization.

improvementPlan.displayText: Protect linear distribution feeds and ad signaling in converged delivery

choices.title: Implement secure data collaboration with least privileged access and privacy controls

helpfulResource.displayText: Advertising measurement, attribution, and audience insights require multiple parties to combine their data. Privacy-preserving collaborating mechanisms help you avoid sharing raw data (privacy riks) forgoing cross-party insights (business cost). Secure data collaboration produces those insights without data exposure.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement secure data collaboration with least privileged access and privacy controls

choices.title: Implement confidential computing for cross-party measurement without exposing raw viewer data

helpfulResource.displayText: Cross-party advertising measurement requires combining datasets from competing parties to answer questions about deduplicated reach, frequency, and attribution. Even with AWS Clean Rooms access controls, some measurement computations require temporary processing of raw data. Confidential computing cryptographically protects raw data during computation. Attestation proves to all parties which code processed their data.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement confidential computing for cross-party measurement without exposing raw viewer data

questions.description: This capability covers network, edge, and request-layer controls. Creative substitution after delivery and changes inside an approved asset belong to content-integrity controls.

helpfulResource.displayText: Advertising platforms process variable traffic loads that can spike by orders of magnitude during live events or tentpole programming. Outside parties might exploit this variability by disguising volumetric events as legitimate bid request traffic. Without threat-aware protection tuned to advertising traffic patterns, systems can't distinguish a real traffic spike from unauthorized traffic without dropping legitimate revenue-generating requests.

improvementPlan.displayText: Protect advertising endpoints against volumetric and application-layer attacks

questions.title: How do you preserve content integrity and guard against unsafe placement, supply-chain fraud, and delivery manipulation?
questions.description: The scope includes malvertising, brand suitability, supply-chain misrepresentation, creative substitution, and fabricated delivery sessions. It doesn't cover volumetric protection at the infrastructure boundary or the privacy terms governing audience data.

choices.title: Validate and sanitize ad creative content before campaign activation

helpfulResource.displayText: Unauthorized ad creatives (malvertising) are a direct security threat to viewers and publishers. Compromised creatives can contain JavaScript-based issues, redirect chains to fraudulent sites, cryptomining code, or forced downloads. Without pre-activation scanning, your service can serve one compromised creative millions of times before you detect it.

improvementPlan.displayText: Validate and sanitize ad creative content before campaign activation

choices.title: Create guardrails and controls to maintain brand safety and content moderation within your workload

helpfulResource.displayText: Ad platforms decide placements faster than people can review content. Without automated classification against your organization's taxonomy, the service can serve ads next to content that violates an advertiser's brand-safety requirements. The taxonomy you designate, and the person who owns it, limit what your service can enforce.

improvementPlan.displayText: Create guardrails and controls to maintain brand safety and content moderation within your workload

choices.title: Implement supply chain transparency controls to block ad fraud

helpfulResource.displayText: Demand-side platforms (DSPs) need to verify in real time that advertisers and agencies purchase legitimate inventory across exchanges. With the IAB Tech Lab transparency stack (ads.txt, sellers.json, app-ads.txt, and the SupplyChain object), DSPs can validate each impression opportunity in the programmatic supply chain.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement supply chain transparency controls to block ad fraud

choices.title: Secure ad creative delivery and content integrity across converged channels

helpfulResource.displayText: Server-side ad insertion (SSAI) dynamically inserts ads into broadcast-grade streams. A threat actor who substitutes a creative can create a large-scale brand safety threat. One compromised creative in a free ad-supported streaming television (FAST) channel or live stream can reach the entire audience at once. Verify integrity from ad decisioning through manifest stitching and viewer delivery.

improvementPlan.displayText: Secure ad creative delivery and content integrity across converged channels

questions.description: This capability also governs the transition away from tracking methods that expose people across contexts. It defines obligations, evidence, permitted use, migration boundaries, and retirement decisions rather than duplicating data-protection or identity mechanisms.

choices.title: Verify that your advertising workload meets applicable data protection obligations

helpfulResource.displayText: Advertising platforms process data across many jurisdictions, business relationships, and delivery channels, and each has obligations from law, contracts, and voluntary frameworks. Adherence to obligations requires tracing each obligation to the data it affects, the purpose it governs, the control that enforces it, and the evidence you kept.

improvementPlan.displayText: Verify that your advertising workload meets applicable data protection obligations

choices.title: Design for compliance across both linear and digital data flows

helpfulResource.displayText: When you design across datasets that can intersect, treat the joined result as its own compliance case. For example, household data and device data might each be fine on their own, but when you match them, they can pinpoint one person. The combined dataset then falls under tighter privacy obligations, even though you followed every rule on either data source.

improvementPlan.displayText: Design for compliance across both linear and digital data flows

helpfulResource.displayText: Advertising platforms need targeting and measurement that don't depend on cross-site or cross-application identification. The migration itself creates risk, as legacy tracking and its replacement can expose the same people through separate data paths.

improvementPlan.displayText: Enable privacy-preserving advertising capabilities while protecting user data

questions.title: How do you design and evolve your advertising workload to be resilient, scalable, and recoverable while managing changes safely?
questions.description: Advertising systems require architectural decisions that determine how failures propagate, how quickly revenue recovers, and whether code changes introduce new failure modes under production traffic. Architecture choices (event-driven compared to synchronous, per-component recovery objectives, and elastic scaling) directly affect whether a single partner outage cascades into total auction failure or is absorbed without revenue impact. Change management choices (testing depth, deployment topology, and rollback authority) determine whether a new release improves reliability or degrades it undetected during peak campaign hours.

improvementPlan.displayText: Deploy partner-facing bid gateways across multiple Availability Zones

questions.title: How do you design and configure your network architecture to meet the performance requirements of your advertising workload?
questions.description: The optimal networking solution for an advertising workload varies based on latency, throughput requirements, jitter, and bandwidth. AWS offers networking features including Amazon Route 53 latency routing, Amazon VPC endpoints, AWS Direct Connect, Amazon CloudFront, and AWS Global Accelerator to reduce network latency and jitter. For advertising workloads, network architecture is more important than in most systems because every ad request depends on a stable network path. A well-designed network directly affects both the performance and the viewer experience of advertising workloads on AWS.

choices.title: Establish private connections between your VPC and AWS services to improve performance

helpfulResource.displayText: Establish private connections between your virtual network and managed cloud services such as object storage, databases, caching, and streaming. Keeping this traffic off the public internet improves security and reduces network hops and latency variability on the critical bid path.

improvementPlan.displayText: Establish private connections between your VPC and AWS services to improve performance

choices.title: Use edge services for static content caching and dynamic request acceleration

helpfulResource.displayText: Cache static advertising content from edge locations near viewers and to route dynamic requests over a backbone network. This reduces latency for ad creative delivery and provides more consistent performance for dynamic advertising requests globally.

improvementPlan.displayText: Use edge services for static content caching and dynamic request acceleration

choices.title: Use load balancers to improve high availability and load distribution

helpfulResource.displayText: Use an elastic load balancer to distribute advertising traffic across healthy targets using algorithms matched to your request patterns. Advertising platforms serve traffic types with different latency and volume characteristics (bid requests, creative assets, and tracking beacons). Isolate these traffic types at the load balancer layer to keep high-volume, latency-tolerant tracking traffic from competing with latency-sensitive bid evaluation for compute.

improvementPlan.displayText: Use load balancers to improve high availability and load distribution

choices.title: Provide dedicated network connection between your on-premises, multicloud environment and AWS

helpfulResource.displayText: Use a dedicated private connection to provide stable and high-speed data communication between on-premises advertising infrastructure and the cloud. Advertising platforms move data at volumes and under regulatory constraints that make public internet transfers inadequate. Behavioral data falls under private network path requirements. Hybrid architectures need on-premises bid decisioning to query cloud-hosted audience data without internet latency variability. For cross-cloud workflows, equivalent private connectivity links separate cloud environments.

improvementPlan.displayText: Provide dedicated network connection between your on-premises, multicloud environment and AWS

choices.title: Use a managed low-latency fabric for real-time bidding infrastructure

AWS RTB Fabric offloads client-side load balancing, TLS termination, and observability to the RTB Fabric Service itself. With Managed Endpoints, RTB Fabric routes bid traffic directly from the responder gateway to individual bidder pod IPs, bypassing the NLB, TLS termination layer, and ingress controller that traditional architectures place on the critical path.

improvementPlan.displayText: Use a managed low-latency fabric for real-time bidding infrastructure

This capability focuses on optimizing real-time bidding systems and media delivery infrastructure where sub-millisecond to single-digit-millisecond latency determines competitive advantage. It covers chipset-agnostic design for Spot cost optimization, network protocol optimization, ARTF agent container performance, Prebid Server auction tuning, SGAI ad break latency optimization, real-time bid stream analytics pipelines, and contextual pre-classification at ingest time.

choices.title: Adopt a chipset-agnostic workload design for best availability of cloud resources and cost

helpfulResource.displayText: Implement an x86 chipset-agnostic design for advertising workloads to optimize Spot Instance compute costs. Spot Instance pricing for AMD and Intel x86 instances fluctuates independently based on capacity supply and demand. Workloads that can run on either chipset consistently select the lower-cost option, which maximizes Spot savings without sacrificing instance availability.

improvementPlan.displayText: Adopt a chipset-agnostic workload design for best availability of cloud resources and cost

choices.title: Optimize your intake request format (HTTP/2 or HTTP/3) for faster processing

helpfulResource.displayText: HTTP/3 with QUIC addresses two performance limitations for advertising workloads that HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 can't solve in transport: connection setup overhead and head-of-line blocking during parallel ad creative delivery.

improvementPlan.displayText: Optimize your intake request format (HTTP/2 or HTTP/3) for faster processing

choices.title: Optimize Agentic RTB Framework (ARTF) agent container performance for sub-millisecond to single-digit-millisecond latency

helpfulResource.displayText: ARTF agent containers process bid requests through gRPC and return OpenRTB Patch mutations under strict auction deadlines. Container image size, startup sequence, serialization format, memory layout, and inference engine affect whether your agent responds within the auction window. ARTF targets sub-millisecond to single-digit-millisecond response times.

improvementPlan.displayText: Optimize Agentic RTB Framework (ARTF) agent container performance for sub-millisecond to single-digit-millisecond latency

choices.title: Optimize Prebid Server adapter concurrency and timeout budgets

helpfulResource.displayText: Prebid Server completes unified header bidding auctions within the publisher-configured auction timeout while maximizing bid density from connected demand partners. improvementPlan.displayText: Optimize Prebid Server adapter concurrency and timeout budgets

choices.title: Minimize SGAI ad break latency with CDN-cached manifests, pre-transcoded creatives, and scaled ADS

helpfulResource.displayText: Ad breaks in SGAI (Server-Guided Ad Insertion) workflows must start with no viewer-perceptible buffering. improvementPlan.displayText: Minimize SGAI ad break latency with CDN-cached manifests, pre-transcoded creatives, and scaled ADS

questions.title: How do you implement cloud financial management practices for your advertising workloads?
questions.description: Maintaining a cost-efficient infrastructure is essential for the profitability of advertising workloads. With fluctuations in usage over time, the costs associated with real-time bidding workloads can vary significantly. Continually monitoring costs is the best way to keep them under control. Evaluate resiliency needs against the cost of downtime for ad delivery and bidding to make proportional investments in reliability. Fragmented measurement across linear TV and digital forces publishers to maintain separate measurement stacks, pay multiple vendors for overlapping capabilities, and run redundant identity resolution processes. Unifying measurement reduces infrastructure duplication while enabling complete reach, frequency, and attribution analysis.

choices.title: Continually measure costs of advertising workloads, and adjust resource and model allocation accordingly

helpfulResource.displayText: With fluctuations in usage over time, the costs associated with advertising workloads can vary significantly. RTB infrastructure costs scale with bid volume and campaign mix. Agentic AI costs scale with agent invocations and token consumption. To keep both under control, monitor them continually with dashboards that correlate spending to business outcomes.

choices.title: Evaluate resiliency needs against the cost of downtime for ad delivery and bidding

helpfulResource.displayText: Compare the cost of running resilient infrastructure against the cost of going without it. With those numbers, you can choose Multi-Region deployments, backup strategies, and recovery approaches that balance cost against business continuity.

improvementPlan.displayText: Evaluate resiliency needs against the cost of downtime for ad delivery and bidding

choices.title: Consolidate identity resolution to reduce redundant matching across linear and digital audiences

helpfulResource.displayText: You pay twice for matching and resolution when you maintain separate identity graphs for linear and digital audiences, often through different vendors with overlapping capabilities. questions.title: How do you select and configure cost-effective compute, storage, and network resources for your advertising workloads?
questions.description: Cost optimization means providing the performance a workload requires at the lowest possible price point, not just reducing spend. For advertising workloads, this means using ARM processors for faster and more cost-effective bidder nodes, compression to reduce network traffic and storage costs, provisioned capacity for predictable workloads, and Spot Instances for fault-tolerant bidding-as-a-service workloads.

choices.title: Use ARM processors for faster and more cost-effective bidder nodes

helpfulResource.displayText: For RTB bidder nodes, ARM-based instances cost less than comparable x86 instances and deliver up to 40 percent better price-performance for supported workloads.

improvementPlan.displayText: Use ARM processors for faster and more cost-effective bidder nodes

choices.title: Use compression to reduce network traffic and storage costs

helpfulResource.displayText: Compression reduces the amount of data you transfer and store, which lowers network and storage costs. Advertising workloads handle large volumes of bid events, impression logs, and creative assets, so applying compression consistently across data paths lowers costs at scale.

improvementPlan.displayText: Use compression to reduce network traffic and storage costs

choices.title: Use provisioned resource allocation for campaigns with predictable capacity, and use dynamic allocation for unexpected capacity

helpfulResource.displayText: Provisioned and on-demand pricing give advertising workloads different cost profiles. Provisioned capacity reserves dedicated resources at a lower cost for each unit and suits predictable workloads. On-demand and serverless capacity cost more per unit but scale freely, which suits unpredictable workloads. Match each component to a suitable model to avoid both overspending and under-provisioning.

Advertising workloads include many interruptible components (batch bid log processing, audience model training, report generation, and A/B test analytics) where Spot Instances save substantial cost when you pair them with fault-tolerance mechanisms.

questions.title: How do you minimize data transfer and communication costs between advertising platform components?
questions.description: Communication between SSPs and DSPs can be significant and can lead to high communication costs. Cross-AZ data transfer charges, internet egress fees, and NAT Gateway processing charges accumulate rapidly at RTB scale. Using private communication channels, co-locating SSP and DSP platforms, and co-locating bidder and database nodes reduces these costs while also improving latency. Beyond connectivity architecture, filtering invalid or non-matching bid requests at the network layer before they reach application compute avoids wasted processing costs. SSPs can shape outbound traffic to suppress requests unlikely to generate bids, and DSPs can optimize no-bid response handling to reduce infrastructure demand. AWS RTB Fabric provides purpose-built infrastructure with transaction-based pricing, built-in traffic filtering modules, Availability Zone affinity, and auto-scaling compute that compounds these savings.

choices.title: Consider private communication channels between SSP and DSP

helpfulResource.displayText: Private communication channels keep traffic secure and reduce internet egress charges. When you connect supply-side and demand-side platforms over private endpoints, bid data stays off the public internet. This practice can improve performance while simplifying network architecture.

improvementPlan.displayText: Consider private communication channels between SSP and DSP

choices.title: Implement Availability Zone affinity across the RTB data path

helpfulResource.displayText: Cross-AZ data transfer charges accumulate at RTB scale into one of the largest line items on an advertising infrastructure bill. Availability Zone affinity keeps all components of a bid request's processing path within a single Availability Zone (such as SSP-to-DSP communication, bidder-to-database queries, caching lookups, and RTB Fabric gateway routing). Intra-AZ traffic over private IP addresses incurs no data transfer charges and has sub-millisecond latency.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement Availability Zone affinity across the RTB data path

choices.title: Filter inbound bid requests at the network layer to reduce compute costs

helpfulResource.displayText: Most DSP bidders respond with no-bid to 70 percent or more of incoming requests. Each no-bid still consumes compute. The request traverses the network, gets deserialized, gets evaluated against targeting logic, and produces a response with zero revenue. If you filter predictably non-viable requests at the network layer before they reach application compute, you avoid that cost entirely. The built-in OpenRTB Filter and Rate Limiter modules in RTB Fabric run this filtering at no additional charge.

improvementPlan.displayText: Filter inbound bid requests at the network layer to reduce compute costs

choices.title: Shape outbound traffic and optimize no-bid handling

helpfulResource.displayText: SSPs pay for every bid request sent regardless of whether a DSP responds with a bid. DSPs pay for every no-bid response returned. Both costs are avoidable when historical data can predict which requests will not generate bids. Shape outbound request traffic by suppressing low-probability requests before transmission, and coordinate with partners to reduce non-viable traffic volume at the source.

improvementPlan.displayText: Shape outbound traffic and optimize no-bid handling

choices.title: Replace per-gigabyte egress with transaction-priced partner connectivity

helpfulResource.displayText: NAT Gateways charge per GB of data processed plus an hourly fee, and that cost compounds at RTB scale. RTB Fabric prices by transaction instead, which matches how RTB revenue works and can cut networking costs by up to 80 percent compared to NAT Gateway-based architectures. Workloads that keep most of their traffic inside the fabric can save at the top of that range or beyond, depending on traffic mix and average bid payload size.

improvementPlan.displayText: Replace per-gigabyte egress with transaction-priced partner connectivity

choices.title: Maximize partner traffic routed inside a managed connectivity fabric

helpfulResource.displayText: Traffic between two RTB Fabric customers costs far less than traffic sent externally, roughly 6.7 to 10 times less per billion transactions depending on Region and volume tier (about 7.5 times for US and EU traffic at the first tier). When you encourage partners to adopt RTB Fabric, both sides save, and those savings grow as more partners join.

improvementPlan.displayText: Maximize partner traffic routed inside a managed connectivity fabric

choices.title: Optimize bid request and response payload sizes to reduce data transfer costs

helpfulResource.displayText: Each RTB transaction includes 2 KiB (2,048 bytes) of data at no charge. Excess payload charges apply only for bytes above this threshold and can be significant at scale. Keeping payloads under 2 KiB avoids excess data transfer charges entirely.

improvementPlan.displayText: Optimize bid request and response payload sizes to reduce data transfer costs

choices.title: Use volume-tier pricing by consolidating traffic

helpfulResource.displayText: RTB Fabric pricing drops sharply after the first 2 trillion transactions per month. When you consolidate traffic from multiple accounts or partners under a single billing entity, you reach lower pricing tiers faster and lower per-transaction costs.

improvementPlan.displayText: Use volume-tier pricing by consolidating traffic

choices.title: Use built-in fabric load balancing instead of dedicated load balancers

helpfulResource.displayText: A managed bidding fabric can distribute traffic to compute instances and container platforms through DNS-based routing. This removes the need for dedicated load balancers, along with their hourly fees and per-LCU charges at high RTB-scale QPS.

improvementPlan.displayText: Use built-in fabric load balancing instead of dedicated load balancers

choices.title: Right-size compute with auto-scaling and serverless containers

helpfulResource.displayText: RTB traffic follows daily patterns and spikes during major content events. Fixed-capacity infrastructure wastes money during low-traffic periods and drops auctions during spikes. Scalable containers match capacity to demand in near real-time, so you pay less for idle compute during nights and weekends.

improvementPlan.displayText: Right-size compute with auto-scaling and serverless containers

questions.title: How do you optimize the cost of database storage and access for your advertising user profile and campaign data?
questions.description: User profile databases tend to be large, holding anywhere from 100-200 million to 5 billion user profiles, and they contain a wide range of data about users' online activities and interactions. Storing and accessing this data can increase cost substantially. How you store, cache, and replicate user profile data directly affects the largest database cost components in RTB architectures. Privacy-enhanced collaboration adds another cost dimension. Collaborative analytics environments price queries by bytes scanned, so data format, partitioning strategy, and query patterns have a direct and multiplicative effect on spend.

choices.title: Consider lower-cost storage for older user profile data

helpfulResource.displayText: Recent user profile data drives bid evaluation, so the last 30 days belong in high-performance storage. Archiving older profiles to low-cost object storage can reduce costs. High-performance database storage costs substantially more per gigabyte than object storage, making tiered storage effective for large-scale user profile stores.

improvementPlan.displayText: Consider lower-cost storage for older user profile data

choices.title: Consider multi-level caching for user profile data

helpfulResource.displayText: A caching layer is a cost-effective way to serve user profile data because it reduces read latency and cuts direct database operations. An in-memory cache holds frequently retrieved items and returns them in microseconds.

improvementPlan.displayText: Consider multi-level caching for user profile data

choices.title: Store profiles in a single Region and replicate asynchronously

helpfulResource.displayText: Users are generally in one Region at a time, so their profiles update in only one Region. You can schedule replication a few times a day using serverless functions and workflow orchestration. This meets resiliency requirements while reducing the replicated write capacity that ongoing cross-region replication consumes.

improvementPlan.displayText: Store profiles in a single Region and replicate asynchronously

questions.title: How do you minimize the cost of agentic AI in advertising, including fraud detection and inference, while maintaining quality?
questions.description: In high-scale adtech environments engineered for low-latency and high-volume operations, fraudulent activity directly amplifies usage across compute, storage, and networking resources. Design fraud detection pipelines to minimize redundant processing and optimize inference costs through caching known outcomes, filtering threats as early as possible, and running only necessary inference steps on cost-efficient compute. Beyond fraud detection, agentic AI advertising workloads on Amazon Bedrock incur costs through foundation model inference, knowledge base retrieval, and multi-agent orchestration. Without ongoing cost monitoring tied to business outcomes, spending grows unchecked as agent usage scales with campaign activity. The highest-impact optimizations are matching model capability to task complexity, optimizing token consumption, and aligning pricing models to invocation patterns.

choices.title: Design fraud detection pipelines to minimize redundant processing and optimize inference costs

helpfulResource.displayText: Design fraud detection workflows that avoid repeated evaluations. Cache known outcomes, filter threats as early as possible, and run only the necessary inference steps on cost-efficient compute resources.

improvementPlan.displayText: Design fraud detection pipelines to minimize redundant processing and optimize inference costs

choices.title: Select the right foundation model for each advertising agent's task complexity

helpfulResource.displayText: Not every advertising agent requires the most capable and expensive foundation model. Matching model capability to task complexity is a high impact cost optimization for agentic AI advertising workloads. Basic classification tasks such as brand safety detection and ad format matching can run on lightweight models at a fraction of the cost of flagship models.

improvementPlan.displayText: Select the right foundation model for each advertising agent's task complexity

choices.title: Implement prompt caching and optimize prompt design to minimize token consumption

helpfulResource.displayText: Advertising agents frequently process similar campaign briefs, audience data schemas, and inventory structures. You reduce token consumption and inference costs by caching common context blocks and designing concise prompts. Prompt caching can reduce costs for cached tokens by up to 90 percent compared to standard input token pricing.

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement prompt caching and optimize prompt design to minimize token consumption

choices.title: Optimize knowledge base indexing frequency and retrieval strategies to minimize costs

helpfulResource.displayText: Advertising agents rely on knowledge bases to hold campaign intelligence, performance analytics, viewer monetization data, and brand safety guidelines. Frequent re-indexing and over-retrieval drive up costs. Configure knowledge bases to sync only when data changes, and keep chunk sizes and retrieval counts at the minimum that maintains quality.

improvementPlan.displayText: Optimize knowledge base indexing frequency and retrieval strategies to minimize costs

choices.title: Design small, focused agents and use appropriate orchestration patterns to minimize multi-agent collaboration costs

helpfulResource.displayText: Each inter-agent call in a multi-agent advertising system incurs additional inference costs. A poorly configured agentic architecture creates excessive handoffs, when instead a deterministic workflow would work better. Design small, focused agents with bounded iteration limits, and replace supervisor agent overhead with deterministic workflows.

improvementPlan.displayText: Design small, focused agents and use appropriate orchestration patterns to minimize multi-agent collaboration costs

helpfulResource.displayText: Provisioned throughput can provide the lowest cost per token for steady-state advertising agents. For unpredictable advertising workloads, on-demand pricing costs less by avoiding idle capacity charges. To reduce cost, match the pricing model to the invocation pattern.

improvementPlan.displayText: Use provisioned throughput for steady-state agents and on-demand pricing for variable workloads

helpfulResource.displayText: Managed model services release new foundation models and cost optimization features regularly. Newer models often match or beat older ones on quality at lower cost. Ongoing evaluation limits resource consumption drift and keeps your advertising agent architecture current.

improvementPlan.displayText: Continuously evaluate new models, features, and pricing options to optimize agentic AI advertising costs over time

questions.title: How do you optimize media delivery and creative costs for your FAST channel and rich-media advertising workloads?
questions.description: FAST channels combine channel assembly from a VOD library with SSAI and SGAI monetization to stream continual linear content. Two cost areas dominate these workloads: delivering the content and serving the ad creative. On the delivery side, the largest saving comes from programmatic channel assembly rather than continual live encoding infrastructure, and VOD storage costs scale with how much of the library each channel actually serves. Balance these costs against ad revenue to maximize revenue per dollar of infrastructure spend. Creative serving has its own costs. Interactive, rich-media, and shoppable formats have larger payloads, render in more complex ways, and cost more to serve than standard display or video ads. When they are not designed with cost in mind, they erode the CPM premium they command. Pre-cache creative assets at the CDN edge and serve formats only to devices that can render them to avoid wasted serving costs.

choices.title: Use programmatic channel assembly to remove dedicated encoding infrastructure

helpfulResource.displayText: Traditional linear channels require live encoding infrastructure that runs around the clock regardless of viewership. Programmatic channel assembly creates linear channels from existing VOD assets without ongoing encoding, which removes the most expensive infrastructure component for back-catalog FAST channels.

improvementPlan.displayText: Use programmatic channel assembly to remove dedicated encoding infrastructure

choices.title: Optimize VOD storage costs for FAST channel source content

helpfulResource.displayText: FAST channels draw from a VOD library with highly variable access patterns. Some titles play daily while others remain idle for weeks. Automatic storage tiering moves objects between access tiers based on access patterns, so storage costs drop without manual management.

improvementPlan.displayText: Optimize VOD storage costs for FAST channel source content

choices.title: Pre-cache creative assets at the CDN edge to avoid redundant origin fetches

helpfulResource.displayText: Innovative ad formats (such as interactive overlays, shoppable ads, and 360 video) have larger creative payloads than standard ads. Fetching the same creative from origin on every impression wastes bandwidth and increases latency. CDN edge caching and pre-fetching avoids redundant origin fetches.

improvementPlan.displayText: Pre-cache creative assets at the CDN edge to avoid redundant origin fetches

choices.title: Use device capability filtering to avoid wasted spend on unsupported formats

helpfulResource.displayText: Sending rich-media creatives to devices that can't render them wastes bandwidth, compute, and ad spend with zero viewer engagement. Capability detection and graceful fallback runs every impression with the best format the device can render.

improvementPlan.displayText: Use device capability filtering to avoid wasted spend on unsupported formats

choices.title: Remove redundant order management systems by unifying campaign booking across buying models

improvementPlan.displayText: Remove redundant order management systems by unifying campaign booking across buying models

questions.title: How do you design your advertising software, architecture, and data lifecycle to minimize resource consumption per unit of work?
questions.description: Design and implement architectures that minimize the average resources (compute, storage, and network) required per unit of work for your advertising workloads. Software and architecture choices directly determine how many resources are consumed to process each bid, deliver each impression, and serve each ad creative. Optimizing these choices reduces environmental impact proportionally with the scale of advertising operations.

choices.title: Run advertising fleets on multiple chipsets, including ARM, to lower energy intensity

helpfulResource.displayText: Advertising workloads such as real-time bidding and creative rendering run on large, elastic, interruption-tolerant fleets. With multi-architecture design, your workload absorbs spare capacity that is already provisioned and powered, instead of triggering new dedicated capacity at a peak. It also runs on the most energy-efficient processor it has a validated build for, where AWS reports that Graviton-based instances use up to 60 percent less energy than comparable EC2 instances for the same performance.

improvementPlan.displayText: Run advertising fleets on multiple chipsets, including ARM, to lower energy intensity

choices.title: Choose HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 to lower bytes transferred and connection overhead

helpfulResource.displayText: Use next-generation networking protocols to address low-latency needs and reduce connection overhead. HTTP/3 with QUIC avoids TCP head-of-line blocking and reduces connection establishment overhead, lowering the compute work and bytes transferred per ad creative delivery. Those quantities are the proxy for the energy attributable to that delivery.

improvementPlan.displayText: Choose HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 to lower bytes transferred and connection overhead

choices.title: Reduce CPU time per bid in agent containers to lower fleet energy intensity

helpfulResource.displayText: ARTF agent containers process bid requests and return OpenRTB Patch mutations under strict auction deadlines. Inefficiency in container image size, memory allocation, serialization, or inference execution increases the CPU time and compute resources each bid consumes. Because compute resource use is the practical proxy for the energy and carbon cost of this workload, containers that complete work in fewer CPU cycles reduce that footprint while also meeting auction deadlines.

improvementPlan.displayText: Reduce CPU time per bid in agent containers to lower fleet energy intensity

choices.title: Tune adapter concurrency and timeouts to stop spending compute on unusable bids

helpfulResource.displayText: Prebid Server completes each header bidding auction within the publisher's timeout and keeps bid density high. When an adapter continually misses the deadline, disable it. This stops the server from spending compute on responses that arrive too late to win.

improvementPlan.displayText: Tune adapter concurrency and timeouts to stop spending compute on unusable bids

choices.title: Serve cacheable ad manifests to reduce origin requests and server-side compute at scale

helpfulResource.displayText: Server-guided ad insertion (SGAI) generates non-personalized media manifests with standard ad markers that a content delivery network can cache and reuse across many viewers. Server-side ad insertion (SSAI), by contrast, stitches a viewer-specific manifest for each session, which defeats shared caching and makes origin load grow with the audience. At live FAST-channel scale, choosing cacheable manifests reduces origin requests and the server-side compute behind them.

improvementPlan.displayText: Serve cacheable ad manifests to reduce origin requests and server-side compute at scale

choices.title: Keep yield analytics off the auction path so its compute scales with events, not traffic

helpfulResource.displayText: Decouple yield analytics from the auction hot path so that analytics compute does not run synchronously in the bid evaluation path. A dedicated streaming pipeline makes bid-level yield data available within a minute of auction completion.

improvementPlan.displayText: Keep yield analytics off the auction path so its compute scales with events, not traffic

choices.title: Classify content once at ingest to remove repeat inference from the auction path

helpfulResource.displayText: Content classification results don't change between one bid request and the next. A classifier invoked during bid evaluation recomputes them anyway, so inference load grows with ad traffic. Classifying each item once at publish time decouples inference from ad traffic.

improvementPlan.displayText: Classify content once at ingest to remove repeat inference from the auction path

choices.title: Identify and remove redundant data across advertising storage infrastructure

helpfulResource.displayText: Participants in the real-time advertising supply chain accrue large volumes of data, much of which serves no lasting purpose. Redundant creatives, expired logs, and superseded artifacts consume storage and the resources behind it long after their value ends. Retaining advertising data only as long as its purpose requires reduces the storage footprint and the energy and carbon associated with it.

improvementPlan.displayText: Identify and remove redundant data across advertising storage infrastructure

questions.title: How do you reduce bid stream resources, from inbound intake to outbound response, on traffic with no advertising value?
questions.description: Waste accumulates on both legs of the bid stream. Some inbound requests a bidder can never act on, some outbound requests a seller should never have sent, most responses carry no bid at all, and every message on the path tends to carry fields and connection overhead that no counterparty needs. Most bid requests never convert to wins: mismatched targeting, depleted budgets, and unsuitable inventory mean these requests consume compute, memory, and network resources without generating value. Each processed request requires energy to power the infrastructure with no environmental return.

choices.title: Reject non-actionable bid requests before they draw compute energy

helpfulResource.displayText: Invalid or incompatible requests waste energy when they reach application compute. You can reduce that waste by rejecting them at the network layer, upstream of compute, which also improves response times.

improvementPlan.displayText: Reject non-actionable bid requests before they draw compute energy

choices.title: Apply rate limiting to control inbound request volume per partner

helpfulResource.displayText: Without rate limits, partner spikes drive unplanned infrastructure scaling and energy draw. Rate limiting caps queries per second per partner connection, which stabilizes resource demand and reduces energy consumption in downstream systems.

improvementPlan.displayText: Apply rate limiting to control inbound request volume per partner

choices.title: Suppress low-probability outbound bid requests to avoid needless compute and network draw

helpfulResource.displayText: You can predict which requests will likely receive bids by mining historical bid and no-bid patterns per DSP. Suppressing them before transmission cuts unnecessary infrastructure use and energy expenditure.

improvementPlan.displayText: Suppress low-probability outbound bid requests to avoid needless compute and network draw

choices.title: Reduce no-bid response volume to lower infrastructure demand and energy draw

helpfulResource.displayText: Real-time bidding produces both winning bids and no-bid responses. Reducing unnecessary no-bid traffic lowers DSP infrastructure demand and energy draw without compromising win rates.

improvementPlan.displayText: Reduce no-bid response volume to lower infrastructure demand and energy draw

choices.title: Minimize bid response payload sizes

helpfulResource.displayText: Oversized bid responses increase network bandwidth demand and processing overhead. Reducing payload sizes lowers data transfer energy consumption and improves system-wide efficiency.

improvementPlan.displayText: Minimize bid response payload sizes

choices.title: Reduce per-auction network overhead by consolidating bid request fan-out and reusing transport connections

helpfulResource.displayText: Programmatic advertising auctions generate network traffic that scales with both the number of concurrent users and the number of demand partners in each auction. How bid requests reach demand partners, and how you manage transport connections, determines whether per-auction network overhead grows with business volume or stays bounded.

improvementPlan.displayText: Reduce per-auction network overhead by consolidating bid request fan-out and reusing transport connections

questions.title: How do you improve infrastructure efficiency when using AWS RTB Fabric for your real-time bidding workloads?
questions.description: Network infrastructure is a major energy consumer for RTB workloads given the transaction volumes exchanged between AdTech partners. AWS RTB Fabric provides purpose-built infrastructure that can reduce resource consumption compared to standard cloud networking.

choices.title: Align partner connectivity capacity with bid activity to reduce idle energy draw

helpfulResource.displayText: NAT gateways continuously process data and consume energy regardless of traffic quality. A transaction-oriented connectivity model matches real-time bidding (RTB) patterns and is more resource-efficient for connectivity to AdTech partners.

improvementPlan.displayText: Align partner connectivity capacity with bid activity to reduce idle energy draw

choices.title: Route more partner traffic internally to share infrastructure and energy savings

helpfulResource.displayText: Traffic exchanged between RTB Fabric customers requires less infrastructure overhead than externally routed traffic. When more partners join RTB Fabric, all participants share the resulting infrastructure and energy savings.

improvementPlan.displayText: Route more partner traffic internally to share infrastructure and energy savings

choices.title: Shed predictably low-value traffic at the network layer to reduce the compute footprint

helpfulResource.displayText: Built-in network-layer modules can filter unwanted traffic without additional infrastructure. Filtering low-value requests early reduces compute resource demand and energy consumption.

improvementPlan.displayText: Shed predictably low-value traffic at the network layer to reduce the compute footprint

choices.title: Carry only the OpenRTB fields the bidding logic uses to reduce bytes on the wire

helpfulResource.displayText: Excess payload adds network bandwidth and energy consumption at scale. Many requests exceed 2 kibibytes (KiB), especially rich video and connected-TV (CTV) bids. The objective is to carry only the fields the bidding logic uses and to reduce payload above the per-transaction allowance.

improvementPlan.displayText: Carry only the OpenRTB fields the bidding logic uses to reduce bytes on the wire

choices.title: Remove dedicated load balancers from the bid path to reduce their idle energy draw

helpfulResource.displayText: A managed bidding fabric can distribute traffic directly to healthy compute targets, using DNS-based routing for compute hosts and managed endpoints for container pods. This removes the need for dedicated load balancers and their ongoing energy draw.

improvementPlan.displayText: Remove dedicated load balancers from the bid path to reduce their idle energy draw

choices.title: Continuously measure fabric utilization and retire unjustified capacity

helpfulResource.displayText: RTB traffic volume, bid rates, and partner mix fluctuate over time, so resource consumption varies with them. Ongoing monitoring shows where you can reduce resources to lower environmental impact.

improvementPlan.displayText: Continuously measure fabric utilization and retire unjustified capacity
